anatomy.intro: Blue-green stem tissue and cream sectors run along the ribs, punctuated by hairy spine cushions.

parts.function: Green living tissue beneath the glaucous surface contributes to photosynthesis.
parts.label: Blue-green stem

parts.function: Paler variegated tissue contains less chlorophyll than neighboring green tissue.
parts.label: Cream sector

parts.function: The small cushion bears spines and fine hairs along the column.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: A raised fold lets the succulent stem accommodate changes in stored water.
parts.label: Rib

flowers.text: White funnel-shaped flowers open at night, sometimes flushed red at the tips, and can be followed by fig-shaped fruits. Studies of Pilosocereus, including P. pachycladus, examine visits by bats, hawkmoths, and bees.

growth.note: Fresh growth extends the column and its color pattern; older plants develop a branching framework.

stages.text: A small plant establishes a ribbed blue-green stem.
stages.title: Young column

stages.text: Fresh growth lengthens the column and carries its own color pattern.
stages.title: Extending tip

stages.text: The normal species can become a large branching cactus tree.
stages.title: Branched framework

habitat.text: Pilosocereus pachycladus is native to eastern Brazil, from the northeast into northern Minas Gerais, in seasonally dry tropical vegetation including the Caatinga. The wild species has blue-green branching columns; the collection's cream sectors are a cultivated variegated feature.

Variegated Pilosocereus pachycladus blue torch cactus: single upright ribbed column with glaucous blue-green waxy surface and broad irregular vertical pale cream-yellow variegated sectors, sparse golden spines on pale fuzzy areoles. 1 points to blue-green stem surface; 2 to a cream-yellow variegated sector; 3 to a pale areole and its spines; 4 to one clearly visible raised vertical rib. No flowers.

lookalikes.name: Golden torch
lookalikes.text: Golden torch is greener with a more uniformly golden spine covering; cream stripes are a feature of this variegated individual.

mature.text: Wild plants can reach as much as 10 m and become branching cactus trees. Cultivated plants remain much smaller.

nameStory.text: Ritter published Pilosocereus pachycladus in 1979. Kew places the familiar trade name Pilosocereus azureus within its subspecies pachycladus.
